frequency_question: How often do legislative resolutions to block executive nuclear or arms agreements successfully pass both chambers and survive or override a presidential veto?
membership_rule: Includes all formal joint resolutions of disapproval introduced against major arms sales or 123 agreements that reached floor votes or serious legislative consideration. Excludes informal expressions of disapproval or resolutions that died in committee without floor action.
provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 major historical showdowns identified where Congress attempted statutory blocking of major executive foreign agreements via disapproval resolutions.
known_gaps: Minor non-statutory resolutions or informal committee blocks are excluded as they do not meet the statutory bar of the resolution criteria.
skeleton: Total major statutory disapproval votes on executive foreign/nuclear agreements since AECA enactment in 1976 versus successful blocks (veto overrides or non-vetoed joint resolutions taking effect).
multiplier: 0 successful blocks out of 4 major legislative showdowns.
validity_reason: The constitutional and statutory balance of power under the AECA and Atomic Energy Act changes slowly and remains anchored in bicameralism and presentment requirements.
